correctness.rationale: Each independent binary tensor sign column is plus or minus exactly one Walsh basis vector, giving an exact multinomial Gram spectrum and inclusion-exclusion full-rank formula. Chernoff upper tails prove sufficiency; a binomial local-mass estimate plus multinomial threshold-indicator negative correlations proves the necessary direction. The finite verifier passed 14,223 exact and exhaustive tests, while strict asymptotic claims are analytic, not inferred from finite runs. Boundary coefficient unproved.

originality.rationale: Exact same-object comparisons show the spectral multinomial identity and sharp all-directions distortion threshold are not obtained by inspected prior statements. The closest source (arXiv:2508.21189, Section 5.3) identifies only a one-vector orthogonality barrier for exactly this factor law; general OSE sufficient bounds and Kronecker zero-testing bounds do not imply the sharp phase constant. Classical Chernoff/occupancy methods are acknowledged as antecedents; residual risk is unindexed equivalent work.
residual_risks: The occupancy large-deviation threshold is a classical type of result; an earlier explicit numerical-sketch specialization might be unindexed or inaccessible.
The broader algorithms studied in the cited papers use different subspace dimensions, factor laws, or distortion notions; these differences are substantive and must remain explicit.
The critical equality regime is not addressed.

value.rationale: A natural published failure model for structured randomized linear algebra is sharpened from a qualitative exponential single-vector barrier to the exact all-vector near-isometry sample constant and a finite spectral law. The near-isometry multiplier \(c_*(1/2)pprox 9.24234\) versus the coupon full-rank multiplier one resolves the algorithmically relevant difference between identifiability and stable embedding. Domain is fixed to binary factors and the full ambient space; no general-purpose complexity promise is asserted.
